state.title: Regression with HTTP `OPTIONS` requests returning 405
state.body:
### What is the issue?

If one uses Ollama HTTP endpoints (`/api/generate` in my particular case) directly from a web page via AJAX or `fetch`, the browser has to issue an `OPTIONS` preflight request as part of the CORS requirements.

In previous versions of Ollama (before the latest released one `0.32.14`, but I can't say which), such `OPTIONS` requests were correctly answered with a `200` and the corresponding headers.  In later releases (and at least in the latest one `0.32.14`), Ollama seems to respond with just `405` and an `Allow: POST` header, which suggests that the `OPTIONS` method was removed.

I have correctly set the `OLLAMA_ORIGINS` environment variable when starting Ollama.

### Relevant log output

Here are the request / response dumps via `tcpdump` pertaining to the `OPTIONS` request described above (redacting the domain that hosts the web page to `<my-site>` and the domain that hosts Ollama to `<my-ollama>`):

```
OPTIONS /api/generate HTTP/1.1
user-agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64; rv:140.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/140.0
accept: */*
accept-language: en-US,en;q=0.5
accept-encoding: gzip, deflate, br, zstd
access-control-request-method: POST
access-control-request-headers: content-type
sec-fetch-dest: empty
sec-fetch-mode: cors
sec-fetch-site: same-site
priority: u=4
[... log trimmed ...]
```

### OS

Linux

### GPU

### CPU

_No response_

### Ollama version

0.32.14

state.title: gemma4:e2b allocates significantly more CUDA_Host memory than VRAM compared to qwen3.5:4b on Windows
state.body:
### What is the issue?

Environment:
- OS: Windows 10
- RAM: 16GB
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti 8GB
- Ollama: 0.32.3
- Model: gemma4:e2b (official)

I noticed that gemma4:e2b allocates most of its model buffer in CUDA_Host (pinned system memory) instead of dedicated VRAM, even though all layers are reported as offloaded to the GPU

For comparison, qwen3.5:4b on the same machine allocates almost all of its model buffer in VRAM and uses very little CUDA_Host memory.

Both models report full GPU offloading (in server.txt - shows "offloaded 36/36" for gemma4:e2b and "offloaded 34/34" for qwen3.5:4b), and inference is fast in both cases. (at least 40tk/s)

Is this expected behavior for Gemma 4 E2B, or could this be a regression?

Steps to reproduce:
1. Pull gemma4:e2b (ollama pull gemma4:e2b)
2. Load gemma4:e2b (ollama run gemma4:e2b)
3. Observe server logs and Windows Task Manager GPU memory
*Note: Even if Dedicated VRAM Usage is ~5GB, RAM used by llama-server is also ~5GB
4. Repeat with qwen3.5:4b

Observed behavior:
- gemma4:e2b uses significantly more CUDA_Host memory than VRAM:
+  CUDA_Host model buffer size = 4795.00MiB
+  CUDA0 model buffer size = 1397.54MiB
- qwen3.5:4b does not show this behavior on the same hardware:
+ CUDA_Host model buffer size = 497.31MiB
+ CUDA0 model buffer size = 2584.74MiB
- with both models, server.txt says "llama_prepare_model_devices: using device CUDA0 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti) - 7126 MiB free"

Expected behavior:
If possible, I would expect gemma4:e2b to utilize dedicated VRAM similarly to qwen3.5:4b when sufficient VRAM is available.

### OS

Windows

### GPU

Nvidia

### CPU

Intel

### Ollama version

0.32.3

state.title: MacOS not saving 0.0.0.0 between hardware restarts
state.body:
### What is the issue?

When I set launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST "0.0.0.0" and restart the Ollama ap everything works as expected and I can access the API from other devices on my network. 

However when I reboot my Mac the OLLAMA_HOST reverts back to 127.0.0.1 and I have to run launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST "0.0.0.0" again.

### What did you expect to see?

When I run launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST "0.0.0.0" and restart my Mac I expected the OLLAMA_HOST to still be set at 0.0.0.0

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run  launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST "0.0.0.0"
2. Restart Ollama App
3. Check the logs to make sure it says "Listening on [::]:11434 (version 0.1.31)"
4. Reboot the Mac
5. Check the logs again and it now says "Listening on 127.0.0.1:11434 (version 0.1.31)"

### Are there any recent changes that introduced the issue?

state.body:
### What is the issue?

**Description:**
Immediately following the release of `v0.32.8`, attempting to pull the corresponding Docker image results in a `manifest unknown` error. This suggests that while the GitHub release tag has been created, the corresponding image tag has not yet been pushed to the Docker registry (Docker Hub).

**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. Run the following command:
   ```bash
   docker pull ollama/ollama:0.32.8
   ```

**Expected Behavior:**
The Docker daemon should locate the `0.32.8` tag and proceed to download the image layers.

**Actual Behavior:**
The pull fails with the following error:
```text
Error response from daemon: manifest for ollama/ollama:0.32.8 not found: manifest unknown: manifest unknown
```

**Environment:**
- **Registry:** Docker Hub (`ollama/ollama`)
- **Context:** Post-release of `v0.32.8`

### Relevant log output

```shell
Error response from daemon: manifest for ollama/ollama:0.32.8 not found: manifest unknown: manifest unknown
```

### OS

Linux

### GPU

Nvidia

### CPU

AMD

### Ollama version

0.32.8

state.title: Solution: AMD 780M iGPU on Linux (systemd) with 32GB RAM.
state.body:
---

**Titel: Lösung: Ollama nutzt AMD iGPU (Ryzen 780M/890M) unter Linux nicht – Fix für systemd (ohne Docker)**

**WICHTIGE VORAUSSETZUNG:**
Diese Lösung ist speziell für Systeme mit **mindestens 32 GB DDR5-RAM** konzipiert. Da die integrierte GPU (iGPU) keinen eigenen Speicher hat, nutzt sie den Systemspeicher als VRAM. Ein 35B-Modell (wie Qwen 3.6) benötigt ca. 24–26 GB Speicher. Auf Systemen mit nur 16 GB RAM führt diese Konfiguration zu Instabilität oder Abstürzen, da nicht genug Speicher für das Modell und das Betriebssystem verbleibt.

**Problem:**
Obwohl die AMD iGPU (Radeon 780M/890M) unter Linux funktioniert und Spiele beschleunigt, nutzt Ollama standardmäßig nur die CPU (`ollama ps` zeigt `100% CPU`). Der Grund: Ollama erkennt die iGPU entweder nicht als unterstütztes Gerät oder ignoriert sie, da der im BIOS reservierte VRAM (oft nur 512 MB) als zu klein eingestuft wird.

**Lösung:**
Anstatt komplexer Skripte oder Docker-Container reicht es, eine systemd-Override-Datei zu erstellen. Diese erzwingt das Vulkan-Backend, erlaubt explizit die Nutzung der iGPU und setzt das VRAM-Limit so hoch, dass der gesamte verfügbare DDR5-RAM (bei 32 GB Systemen) genutzt werden kann.

**Schritt-für-Schritt-Anleitung:**

1.  **Verzeichnis erstellen:**
    ```bash
    sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d
    ```

2.  **Override-Datei erstellen/bearbeiten:**
    Öffne die Datei mit einem Editor (z.B. nano):
    ```bash
    sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/override.conf
    ```

3.  **Inhalt einfügen (Der entscheidende Teil):**

Füge exakt diesen Block ein. Die Zeile `OLLAMA_MAX_VRAM` ist hierbei der Schlüssel, damit Ollama den gesamten RAM als VRAM akzeptiert und nicht am kleinen BIOS-Limit scheitert.
    ```ini
    [Service]
    # Vulkan-Backend erzwingen (wichtig für AMD APUs unter Linux)
    Environment="OLLAMA_VULKAN=1"
    
    # Explizit erlauben, dass integrierte GPUs (iGPUs) genutzt werden
    Environment="OLLAMA_IGPU_ENABLE=1"
    
    # Maximales VRAM-Limit auf ~32GB setzen (in Bytes).
    # WICHTIG: Nur anwenden, wenn das System tatsächlich 32 GB RAM oder mehr hat!
    # Bei 16 GB Systemen diesen Wert auf ca. 10000000000 (10GB) setzen, 
    # aber beachte, dass große Modelle (35B) dann nicht mehr passen.
[... log trimmed ...]
    ```
    *(Speichern mit `STRG+O`, Bestätigen mit `Enter`, Beenden mit `STRG+X`)*

4.  **Dienst neu laden und starten:**
    ```bash
    sudo systemctl daemon-reload
    sudo systemctl restart ollama
    ```

5.  **Überprüfung:**
    Starte ein Modell (z.B. `ollama run DEIN_MODELL_NAME`) und prüfe in einem zweiten Terminal den Status:
    ```bash
    ollama ps
    ```
    **Erfolg:** Unter `PROCESSOR` sollte nun eine Aufteilung wie `43%/57% CPU/GPU` oder ähnlich stehen.

**Hinweis:**
Diese Lösung funktioniert für die native Linux-Installation von Ollama. Für Docker-Nutzer müssen diese Variablen in der `docker-compose.yml` unter `environment:` eingetragen werden. Die Variable `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_ [...]

state.title: Agent integrations hang indefinitely with local Qwen models on macOS, while Ollama API works correctly
state.body:
### What is the issue?

Description

I’m having an issue with local Qwen models on Ollama on macOS.

The models work correctly when calling Ollama directly, including the OpenAI-compatible API, streaming, reasoning, and tool calling.

However, agent integrations consistently hang indefinitely / eventually timeout when using the same models.

I reproduced the issue with multiple independent integrations:

* Pi
* OpenCode
* Claude Code
* Hermes
• qwen
I have not tested others but I guess its same issue.

All of them exhibit essentially the same behavior.

Environment

* macOS 15.7.7 (24G720)
* Apple M3 Max
* 64 GB RAM
* Ollama 0.32.13

Models tested:

* qwen3.8:27b-mlx
* qwen3.8:27b-mxfp8

The problem occurs with both models, so it does not appear to be specific to the MLX backend.

What works

The native Ollama API works correctly:

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/chat \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.8:27b-mlx",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}],
    "stream": false
  }'

This returns a normal response.

The OpenAI-compatible API also works:

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.8:27b-mlx",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}
    ],
    "stream": false
  }'

This also returns correctly.

Streaming works

I also tested:

/v1/chat/completions
stream: true

and Ollama correctly streams:

* reasoning tokens
* normal content tokens
* finish_reason: "stop"
* [DONE]

Tool calling works

I tested a function tool through the OpenAI-compatible API.

Ollama correctly returns:

"tool_calls": [
  {
    "id": "call_2fmw5mg5",
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
      "name": "get_weather",
      "arguments": "{\"city\":\"Paris\"}"
    }
  }
]

with:

"finish_reason": "tool_calls"

I then tested a complete second turn by sending:

1. the original user message
2. the assistant tool_calls message
3. the tool result
4. the tools definition

Ollama successfully generated the final answer.

So the basic OpenAI-compatible agent workflow works when tested directly.

What does NOT work

Despite the above, all of these integrations hang indefinitely when configured to use the same local Ollama models:

Pi       → hangs
OpenCode → hangs
Claude Code → hangs
Hermes   → hangs

The behavior is essentially the same: the model is loaded, the connection is established, but the agent never receives a usable response and eventually appears to timeout.

I also tested both:

qwen3.8:27b-mlx
qwen3.8:27b-mxfp8

with the same result.

I also tested with reasoning enabled and disabled (reasoning_effort: "none"), with no change.

Important observation

This seems to rule out:

* the model failing to load
* the Ollama server being unreachable
* /api/chat being broken
* /v1/chat/completions being broken
* SSE streaming being broken
* basic tool calling being broken
* the MLX model specifically being broken
* [...]

state.title: gemma4: tool calls with 47+ string values are always dropped — placeholder index 44 (`,`) collides in `gemma4ArgsToJSON`
state.body:
### What is the issue?

With any Gemma 4 model, a tool call whose arguments contain more than ~45 string values in a list (for example a
table written as `rows: [[string, string, string], ...]` with 16+ rows) is never returned. The model generates the
call correctly, the parser fails, the call is dropped, and the client gets a message with no content and no
`tool_calls`. The server log shows, at WARN:

```
msg="gemma4 tool call parsing failed" error="invalid character '\x00' looking for beginning of value
repair failed to produce valid JSON arguments"
```

Reproduced on v0.34.2 (Linux, CUDA) with gemma4 e2b, e4b, 12b and 26b-a4b. The same code is on `main` today.

### Suggested fix (3 lines)
Use a decimal index and distinct start/end bytes. Digits are never JSON structure, and with different start and
end bytes the text between two placeholders (`"\x01" + sep + "\x00"`) can never form one. `json.Marshal` escapes both
bytes, so restored strings cannot create a placeholder either.

```diff
@@ import (
 	"regexp"
+	"strconv"
 	"strings"
@@ func gemma4ArgsToJSON(s string) string {
-		return "\x00" + string(rune(len(quotedStrings)-1)) + "\x00"
+		return "\x00" + strconv.Itoa(len(quotedStrings)-1) + "\x01"
 	})
@@
-		text = strings.ReplaceAll(text, "\x00"+string(rune(i))+"\x00", string(escaped))
+		text = strings.ReplaceAll(text, "\x00"+strconv.Itoa(i)+"\x01", string(escaped))
[... log trimmed ...]
```shell

```

state.title: cuda_v12 returns poor results or crashes for Driver Version: 525.147.05
state.body:
### What is the issue?

Between 0.3.7-rc5 and 0.3.7-rc6 the default CUDA driver was switched from v11 to v12 and results from a variety of models degraded.  I first noticed this with 0.3.7-rc6 but the problem also exists in -rc4 if OLLAMA_LLM_LIBRARY is set to cuda_v12.  The problem persists into 0.3.8. 

```
$ for l in cuda_v11 cuda_v12 ; do for m in hermes3:8b-llama3.1-q4_0 llama3.1 qwen2:1.5b ; do echo $l $m ; OLLAMA_LLM_LIBRARY=$l OLLAMA_DOCKER_TAG=0.3.8 docker compose up -d ollama 2>/dev/null && sleep 2 && curl -s localhost:11434/api/chat -d '{"model":"'$m'","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say 'hello'"}],"stream":false}' | jq '{"response":"\(.message.content)","error":"\(.error)"}' ; done ; done
cuda_v11 hermes3:8b-llama3.1-q4_0
{
  "response": "\nHello! How can I assist you today?",
  "error": "null"
}
cuda_v11 llama3.1
{
  "response": "Hello! How can I assist you today?",
  "error": "null"
}
[... log trimmed ...]
```

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.147.05   Driver Version: 525.147.05   CUDA Version: 12.0     |
|-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| Fan  Temp  Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap|         Memory-Usage | GPU-Util  Compute M. |
|                               |                      |               MIG M. |
|===============================+======================+======================|
|   0  NVIDIA GeForce ...  Off  | 00000000:01:00.0 Off |                  N/A |
| 30%   44C    P8     8W / 200W |   6251MiB / 12282MiB |      0%      Default |
|                               |                      |                  N/A |
+-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
[... log trimmed ...]
```

The problem does not occur on systems with more recent Nvidia drivers (`NVIDIA-SMI 535.183.01 Driver Version: 535.183.01 CUDA Version: 12.2`, `NVIDIA-SMI 550.90.07 Driver Version: 550.90.07 CUDA Version: 12.4`):
```
cuda_v11 hermes3:8b-llama3.1-q4_0
{
  "response": "\nHello! How can I assist you today?",
  "error": "null"
}
cuda_v11 llama3.1
{
  "response": "Hello! How can I assist you today?",
  "error": "null"
}
cuda_v11 qwen2:1.5b
[... log trimmed ...]
```

This is more of a FYI since it can be worked around by setting OLLAMA_LLM_LIBRARY or (hopefully, I have yet to try) upgrading the nvidia driver.

Docker

### GPU

Nvidia

### CPU

Intel

### Ollama version

0.3.8

state.body:
### What is the issue?

# Bug report: long-lived runner (keep_alive -1) produces corrupted output (repeated placeholder tokens) after coexisting with a second model; fixed only by fully stopping and reloading the runner

---

## Environment

- **Hardware:** GMKtec EVO-X2 Mini PC — AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 ("Strix Halo"), Radeon 8060S iGPU (RDNA 3.5, gfx1151), 128GB LPDDR5X-8000 unified memory
- **OS:** Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel 7.0
- **GPU driver:** ROCm via AMD's repo installer, `amdgpu-install` 31.50 series (`--usecase=rocm --no-dkms`)
- **Ollama config:** `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1` (models stay resident  indefinitely once loaded), `OLLAMA_MODELS=/opt/ollama-models` (internal  NVMe), unified-memory GRUB tuning (`amdgpu.gttsize=120000`,  `ttm.pages_limit=31457280`) — 128GB fully exposed to OS, confirmed via  `dmesg`/`free -h`
- **Fill in before filing:** `ollama -v`, exact `rocm-smi` driver version

## Models involved

- **`gemma4-e4b-agentic:latest`** — custom model, `FROM gemma4:e4b` +  `PARAMETER num_ctx 65536` (no other parameter overrides in the final,  clean-when-isolated build). No speculative decoding for this model  (confirmed absent from its own load log).
- **`qwen3.6-agentic:latest`** — custom model, `FROM qwen3.6:27b`. Uses speculative decoding (`--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3  --spec-draft-backend-sampling`), confirmed present in its load log.
- Both loaded via the standard `ollama create <name> -f Modelfile` flow,  both use `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1`.

## Summary

After `gemma4-e4b-agentic` and `qwen3.6-agentic` were both loaded and active in the same Ollama instance (concurrently sharing the GPU/unified memory pool), `gemma4-e4b-agentic` began returning corrupted output — long repeated runs of a single placeholder token (`<unused49>`) instead of real text — for every subsequent request. This persisted even after `ollama ps` showed only `gemma4-e4b-agentic` still loaded (the other model was no longer listed), meaning the corruption outlived the concurrent period and lived in `gemma4-e4b-agentic`'s own long-running runner process/slot state. The only fix found was to fully stop that runner (`ollama stop gemma4-e4b-agentic`) and let a fresh `ollama run` reload it from scratch — after which output was immediately clean and correct again.

## What was ruled out first (to save reviewers time)

Before concluding this was a concurrency/runner-state bug, the following were tested and eliminated as causes:

1. **Corrupted model conversion / GGUF weights.** Ruled out: after    recreating `gemma4-e4b-agentic` fresh from the base `gemma4:e4b` tag, it produced correct output *in isolation* (see reproduction steps). 
2. **`num_ctx=65536` itself.** Ruled out via direct API call: `curl   .../api/generate` against the clean base `gemma4:e4b` with `"options": {"num_ctx": 65536}` explicitly set — output remained  correct. So the large context parameter alone isn't the trigger.
3. **A malformed special-token in the base GGUF.** The loader does log  [...]

state.title: Support Ticket: Ollama restarts when internet connection drops (session lost)
state.body:
### What is the issue?

---

### 📌 **Support Ticket: Ollama restarts when internet connection drops (session lost)**  

**Subject:** Ollama restarts and loses session when internet connection drops  

**Description of the Problem:**  
When the internet connection is unstable or drops, Ollama restarts and loses the current session (e.g., loaded model, chat history, etc.). This causes data loss and requires the user to restart the process manually.  

**Steps to Reproduce:**  
1. Run Ollama with a model (e.g., `ollama run llama3`).  
2. The internet connection is interrupted (e.g., due to router failure or ISP issues).  
3. Ollama restarts and loses the session.  

**Expected Behavior:**  
- Ollama should retain the session after reconnecting (e.g., by persisting model and session data locally).  
- Alternatively, support an **offline mode** or **persistent storage** for models and session data to prevent restarts.  

**System Information:**  
-

**Additional Notes:**  
- Currently, models are loaded from the network, which causes restarts when the connection drops.  
- Local model storage (e.g., via `ollama pull`) resolves this, but session data is not persisted.  

**Request:**  
Could you implement an **offline mode** or **persistent session storage** to address this issue?  

---

state.title: minicpm5-2b native tool calls never parse
state.body:
### What is the issue?

With `tools` passed to `/api/chat` (and `/v1/chat/completions`), MiniCPM5-2B attempts the native XML tool call, but the response always has `tool_calls: null` (native) / missing (OpenAI compat) and `content` contains a mangled fragment such as ` name="get_weather"> name="city">Paris`. The model reasoning (`thinking`/`reasoning`) shows correct tool intent. Standard clients that branch on `tool_calls` or `finish_reason: tool_calls` never take the tool branch. `finish_reason`/`done_reason` is always `stop`.

repro:
```bash
curl http://localhost:11434/api/chat -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model": "minicpm5-2b:latest",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Paris? Use the tool."}],
  "stream": false,
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather",
    "description": "Get weather for a city",
    "parameters": {"type": "object",
      "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
      "required": ["city"]}}}]
}'
```

response:
```json
{"model":"minicpm5-2b:latest",
 "message":{"role":"assistant",
  "content":" name=\"get_weather\"> name=\"city\">Paris",
  "thinking":"The user wants to know the weather in Paris. I need to use the get_weather function.\n"},
 "done":true,"done_reason":"stop"}
```

`tool_calls` is `null`. OpenAI compat (`/v1/chat/completions`) returns the same mangled `content`, a correct `reasoning` field, no `tool_calls`, `finish_reason: stop`.

upstream reference:
- vLLM `minicpm5xml_tool_parser.py`: "Tool XML tags are special tokens in MiniCPM5; must not strip them before tool parsing ... `request.skip_special_tokens = False`."
- SGLang documents `--tool-call-parser minicpm5` for MiniCPM5-1B XML tool calls.
- OpenBMB/MiniCPM states SGLang is the recommended backend for MiniCPM5 tool calling.

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### OS

Windows

### GPU

Nvidia

### CPU

Intel

### Ollama version

0.30.8

state.title: Ollama 0.32.5 GPT-OSS Q8 Crash Report
state.body:
### What is the issue?

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
# Modelfile
FROM "gpt-oss-20b-UD-Q8_K_XL.gguf"
TEMPLATE """..."""
PARAMETER num_ctx 131072
PARAMETER num_predict 8192
PARAMETER num_batch 1024

ollama create gpt-oss-test -f Modelfile
ollama run gpt-oss-test "hello"
```

### Expected Behavior
Model loads and responds normally (worked on 0.32.4 and 0.32.1).

### Actual Behavior

**With `ollama run`:**
```
500 Internal Server Error: llama-server process has terminated
exit status 0xc0000409: stack-based buffer overrun
GGML_ASSERT(...)
```

**With `ollama serve` + app:**
```
ggml_gallocr_reserve_n_impl: failed to allocate CUDA0 buffer of size 140301549824
cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
```

### Key Findings

1. **Regression from 0.32.1** — The exact same Modelfile and GGUF worked on 0.32.1
2. **Only affects GPT-OSS Q8** — Qwen3.6 Q4, Qwen3.5 Q4, Gemma4 Q5 all work fine with same context settings
3. **Not caused by:** num_predict, temperature, top_k, top_p, or system prompt content
4. **Ollama 0.32.x changed VRAM allocation logic** (PR #14116) — likely related
5. **`OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0` workaround** gets past the OOM but then crashes with stack buffer overrun
6. **Community reports** of similar issues with Q8 models on 0.32.x (Issue #14426, #13863)

### Workaround

- Use Ollama 0.32.1 and 0.32.4 (last known working version for this model)

### Additional Context

Four other models (Qwen3.6, Qwen3.5, Gemma4 — all Q4/Q5) with identical Modelfile structure and 256K context work perfectly on 0.32.5. Only GPT-OSS Q8_K_XL exhibits this crash.

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### OS

Windows

### GPU

Nvidia

### CPU

Intel

### Ollama version

0.32.5

state.title: Ollama Issue Report: AMD Strix Halo (Radeon 8060S) VRAM Detection Failure with ROCm
state.body:
### What is the issue?

Issue Summary
AMD Strix Halo (Radeon 8060S / gfx1151) systems incorrectly report only 2.0 GiB available VRAM instead of the full unified memory (96-114 GiB) when using Ollama with ROCm backend. The issue appears to be a regression introduced between version 0.24.0 and 0.30.x, and also occurs with Vulkan backend detection.
Environment Information

Component | Detail
-- | --
Hardware | AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 with Radeon 8060S Graphics (Strix Halo)
GPU Architecture | gfx1151 (RADV GFX1151)
Total Memory | 114.0 GiB (unified memory)
OS | Linux (Fedora CoreOS / Ubuntu)
Kernel | 6.17.0-23-generic
Ollama Version | 0.30.x (tested up to 0.30.11)
Working Version | 0.24.0-rocm

From journalctl -u ollama.service -f:
time=2026-07-23T20:55:30.430+08:00 level=INFO source=types.go:32 msg="inference compute" id=0 filter_id=0 library=Vulkan compute=0.0 name=Vulkan0 description="AMD Radeon 8060S Graphics (RADV GFX1151)" libdirs=ollama,vulkan driver=0.0 pci_id=0000:c6:00.0 type=iGPU total="111.5 GiB" available="111.3 GiB"

Wait — this log actually shows correct detection (111.3 GiB available). The issue occurs in specific configurations:
Container Deployment (0.30.2-rocm)
time=... level=INFO source=types.go:32 msg="inference compute" id=0 library=ROCm compute=gfx1151 name=ROCm0 description="Radeon 8060S Graphics" libdirs=ollama,rocm_v7_2 driver=0.0 pci_id=0000:c3:00.0 type=iGPU total="113.5 GiB" available="2.0 GiB"

Note: available="17.8 GiB" actually reflects system RAM free space, not VRAM, as confirmed by rocm-smi --showmeminfo vram showing 76+ GiB free. 

Working Version (0.24.0-rocm)
time=... level=INFO source=types.go:42 msg="inference compute" id=0 library=ROCm compute=gfx1151 name=ROCm0 description="Radeon 8060S Graphics" libdirs=ollama,rocm driver=70253.21 pci_id=0000:c3:00.0 type=iGPU total="114.0 GiB" available="113.8 GiB"

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### OS

Linux

### GPU

AMD

### CPU

AMD

### Ollama version

 0.32.0

state.title: `ollama pull` from HF repo fails with bare "Error: 400:" while translating Ollama-format qwen35 mmproj
state.body:
### What is the issue?

## What happened

Pulling `hf.co/llmfan46/Qwen3.6-27B-uncensored-heretic-v2-GGUF:Q4_K_M` downloads
all layers successfully (16.5 GB model GGUF + 931 MB vision projector), then
fails at the create/assembly step with a bare error and no message:

```
pulling c5c8c41da6d1: 100% ▕██████████▏ 931 MB
pulling 6db07cd2f395: 100% ▕██████████▏   57 B
Error: 400:
```

The HTTP layer reports 200 (the error is embedded in the /api/pull stream), and
the server journal shows the failure happens while translating the repo's
vision projector, with no error logged:

```
handle_qwen35_like_clip: detected Ollama-format qwen35 GGUF used as mmproj; translating
load_hparams: projector:          qwen3vl_merger
compat tensor transform: op=concat sources tensor=v.blk.10.attn_qkv.bias ... total_ops=32 total_bytes=105540096
[GIN] ... | 200 | ... | POST "/api/pull"
```

Retried multiple times across two versions — deterministic, not transient.

## What I expected

Either a successful import (the base `qwen3.6:27b` library model imports and
runs fine on the same machine, including vision), or a 400 with an actual error
message saying what is wrong with the projector.

## Workaround that confirms the model itself is fine

Creating from the cached model blob with a bare Modelfile (`FROM <blob path>`,
no projector) succeeds and the model runs correctly — text-only. So the
failure is specific to the mmproj translation path.

## Environment

- Ollama 0.32.4 (also reproduced on the previous installed release)
- Ubuntu, Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 128 GB unified memory
- Model: hf.co/llmfan46/Qwen3.6-27B-uncensored-heretic-v2-GGUF:Q4_K_M
  (repo ships an Ollama-format mmproj: Qwen3.6-27B-mmproj-BF16.gguf)

### Relevant log output

```shell
N/A
```

### OS

Linux

### GPU

AMD

### CPU

AMD

### Ollama version

0.32.4

state.title: glm-5.2:cloud May Have Suffered Significant Intelligence Degradation
state.body:
### What is the issue?

Before the 15th of this month (July) or so, the cloud-hosted glm-5.2 model was performing normally. At least when I used Oh My Pi for programming, it could edit files with basically no errors.

But within a few days, the situation deteriorated significantly. I first noticed this when glm-5.2 started messing up my working directory. Unfortunately, I was in the middle of a large-scale code refactoring with glm at the time, and by the time I realized it, nearly a quarter of the files were corrupted. I had to roll back to the last commit.

I then began restricting the use of sub-agents and monitoring its actual behavior. I found that glm failed to edit correctly or made erroneous edits roughly half the time (adding or deleting lines of code incorrectly—quite destructive). Oh My Pi uses the hashline method for file editing operations (which I think is a relatively new editing tool pattern that may not have been sufficiently reinforced in glm-5.2's training). Even so, **previously** everything worked fine.

After a bad edit, it sometimes detected the mistake and would mutter to itself about fixing the previous edit and then recover (though occasionally it would mess up again). Other times it completely ignored the editing errors, which ultimately led to about a quarter of the files being contaminated.

A while ago, I observed that the output speed of glm-5.2 on Ollama had noticeably increased. I remember being pleased at the time (because it was truly lightning fast). I don't know if the two are related, but this editing issue is fatal. I had OMP switch to apply_patch editing mode to improve success rates, but there is still roughly a 1 in 8 chance of missing a single line, a closing bracket, etc.

My expectations are not high: just stable editing. I believe this is a reasonable expectation for a model with an AA intelligence index approaching 51. I have also used the official model API before (its reasoning was significantly longer), and I think some gap is normal, and to some extent degradation is acceptable (after all, the official version has degraded before). But please, do not degrade to the point where it cannot even complete edits reliably: that is a bit too much.

PS: Or could this be an OMP issue? I checked the relevant Issue, but it actually seems to confirm the suspicion of degradation: https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/3772#issuecomment-4838774245

Edit: I don't know whether you're using quantized models, but just in case you are, please use the UD (dynamic quantization) version provided by Unsloth—this is my sincere wish.

I have used Unsloth's quantized models, and they are noticeably better than other versions. Moreover, they are quite **responsible**: for every quantized release, they do their utmost to eliminate inconsistencies with the original model, and sometimes they even help point out issues in the original release (such as the FP16 precision problem with Gemma 3). I personally trust them a great [...]

state.title: MLX vision runner requests ~125GB Metal buffer (crash) on high-resolution image input with Qwen3.8-27B
state.body:
**Ollama version:** 0.32.13
**Hardware:** MacBook Pro, Apple M5 Pro, 48GB unified memory
**OS:** macOS 26.6.1 (build 25G76)
**Model:** Qwen3.8-27-mlx-nv4-thinking:latest
## What happened
Vision inference on a 5712×4284 (24.5MP) JPEG produced:

Error: 500 Internal Server Error: mlx runner failed: panic: mlx: [metal::malloc] Attempting to allocate 133872076800 bytes which is greater than the maximum allowed buffer size of 30150672384 bytes. at /Users/runner/work/ollama/ollama/build/darwin-sources/_deps/mlx-c-src/mlx/c/transforms.cpp:73

133,872,076,800 bytes (≈124.7 GiB) requested vs a ~28.1 GiB per-buffer Metal cap.
## Repro
1. Attach a 5712×4284 image to a vision request against `Qwen3.8-27-mlx-nv4-thinking:latest`
2. Crash occurs during vision inference
## Workaround
Resizing the same image to 1568px on the longest edge (`sips -Z 1568`) avoids the crash; inference completes normally.
## Suspected cause (unconfirmed)
Vision token count appears to scale directly with raw input resolution rather than being capped before patchification (e.g. a missing `max_pixels`-style resize step). Rough patch math for 5712×4284 at 14px patches (~124,850 tokens) is roughly consistent in magnitude with the requested allocation, suggesting an uncapped self-attention matrix over vision tokens. Not verified against the actual MLX vision preprocessing code.
## Expected behaviour
Large images should be downscaled before patchification (or oversized inputs rejected with a clear error) rather than the runner attempting an allocation this size.

state.title: ollama's NVML queries fail with the 580.xx driver
state.body:
The issue is that ollama's NVML queries fail with the 580.xx driver, causing total_vram="0 B" during GPU discovery. This prevents any GPU layer offloading.

  What we tried:
  1. ✅ Added LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/ollama to service override
  2. ✅ Added ollama user to video and render groups
  3. ✅ Rebuilt ollama-cuda against CUDA 13.0
  4. ❌ None fixed the VRAM detection

  Root cause: Ollama's GPU discovery code uses NVML library calls that don't work properly with the new 580.xx driver (CUDA 13.0). The CUDA backend loads correctly later, but the initial GPU detection fails.

state.title: [Bug]: Cannot load Qwen3.5 models on v0.32.14 with Vulkan backend (Error: 500 Internal Server Error)
state.body:
### What is the issue?

I am unable to run any Qwen3.5 model (e.g., `qwen3.5:0.8b`) using Ollama `v0.32.14` with the Vulkan backend. The server returns a `500 Internal Server Error`, and the logs indicate that the `llama-server` process terminates during model loading.

The specific error in the logs is:
```
Error: 500 Internal Server Error: llama-server process has terminated: exit status 1: error: Failed to load CLIP model from C:\Users\fufu\.ollama\models\blobs\sha256-afb707b6b8fac6e475acc42b
error loading model: error loading model hyperparameters: key qwen35.rope.dimension_sections has wrong array length; expected 4, got 3
```

This model (`qwen3.5:0.8b`) was working correctly on an older version of Ollama (e.g., `v0.17.x`), so this appears to be a regression introduced in a newer version.

**System Information**
- **Ollama version:** 0.32.14
- **Backend:** Vulkan
- **GPU:** "AMD Radeon 760M Graphics with 10GB VRAM
- **System RAM:** 12GB
- **OS:** Windows

**Steps to Reproduce**
1.  Install Ollama `v0.32.14`.
2.  Pull a Qwen3.5 model, e.g., `ollama pull qwen3.5:0.8b`.
3.  Attempt to run the model, e.g., `ollama run qwen3.5:0.8b`.
4.  Observe the `500 Internal Server Error`.

**Expected Behavior**
The model should load and run successfully, as it did on older versions of Ollama.

**Actual Behavior**
The model fails to load with the `qwen35.rope.dimension_sections` error, and the runner process terminates.

**Additional Context**

This error is a known compatibility issue between Ollama's exported GGUF files for Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6 models and the `llama.cpp` loader. The root cause is that Ollama exports the `qwen35.rope.dimension_sections` parameter with **3 entries** `[11, 11, 10]`, but `llama.cpp` expects **4 entries** `[11, 11, 10, 0]`.

state.title: qwen3-vl:8b ignores think=false and /set nothink, streaming never emits content
state.body:
### What is the issue?

## Environment

- Ollama: 0.30.7
- OS: Linux
- API: OpenAI-compatible (/v1/chat/completions)

Model:

```
qwen3-vl:8b
```

## Problem

`qwen3-vl:8b` appears to ignore both:

- `/set nothink`
- `"think": false`

When using streaming, the model continuously emits `reasoning` tokens but never emits any `content`.

Eventually the stream finishes with:

```json
finish_reason: "length"
```

without producing any visible answer.

The same environment works correctly with `qwen3.5:9b`.

## Reproduction

Streaming request:

```bash
curl -N http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{
  "model":"qwen3-vl:8b",
  "stream":true,
  "max_tokens":64,
  "messages":[
    {
      "role":"user",
      "content":"hola"
    }
[... log trimmed ...]
```

Output:

- only `reasoning`
- `content` remains empty
- finishes with

```json
{
  "finish_reason":"length",
  "content":""
}
```

## think=false

```bash
curl http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{
  "model":"qwen3-vl:8b",
  "think":false,
  "messages":[
    {
      "role":"user",
      "content":"hola"
    }
  ]
[... log trimmed ...]
```

The response still contains a populated `reasoning` field.

## CLI

```
>>> /set nothink
Set 'nothink' mode.

After that:

```
>>> hola
```

The model still enters:

```
Thinking...
<think>
...
</think>
```

## Comparison

Exactly the same commands using

```
qwen3.5:9b
```

correctly disable thinking and immediately produce an answer.

This suggests a model-specific issue affecting qwen3-vl:8b.

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### OS

Linux, Docker

### GPU

Nvidia

### CPU

AMD

### Ollama version

0.30.7

state.title: GPU Crashes with "killed entity" errors on AMD RX 7900 XTX with newer kernels
state.body:
### What is the issue?

**Problem Description**
Ollama causes repeated GPU crashes with amdgpu driver errors when running LLM inference. The GPU enters a "killed entity" state, preventing further job submissions. The system remains functional but GPU acceleration fails.

**Steps to Reproduce**
1. Start ollama service
2. Run LLM inference: ollama run _any_model_ (for example `ollama run qwen3:30b`)
3. Start conversation
4. GPU crashes occur after 3 to 10 messages

**Expected Behavior**
Ollama should utilize GPU acceleration without causing driver-level crashes or "killed entity" states.

**Actual Behavior**
GPU repeatedly enters killed state, requiring system reboot to restore GPU functionality. Ollama cannot continue inference after the first crash.

**Workaround**
Ollama Version 0.12.3

### Relevant log output

```shell
amdgpu: Freeing queue vital buffer 0x7f9bcc200000, queue evicted
[drm:amdgpu_job_submit [amdgpu]] *ERROR* Trying to push to a killed entity
```

### OS

Linux Fedora 42, Kernel 6.16.10-200.fc42.x86_64

### GPU

AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (Navi 31, RDNA3, gfx1030)
Driver: amdgpu (Mesa)

### CPU

AMD Ryzen 5 2600X

### Ollama version

0.12.5, 0.12.6, 0.12.7, 0.12.8

state.title: `/api/generate` with `think:true` leaks Qwen reasoning into `response`, while `/api/chat` separates it
state.body:
### What is the issue?

On Ollama 0.34.0, the official `qwen3:14b` model declares the `thinking` capability, but a non-streaming `/api/generate` request with top-level `"think": true` returns the complete `<think>...</think>` block inside `response` and leaves `thinking` empty.

The equivalent `/api/chat` request correctly returns the reasoning in `message.thinking` and only the final answer in `message.content`.

Both requests below are deterministic, use the same model, prompt, seed, temperature, and output limit, and finish normally with `done_reason: "stop"`. No request-level `stop` option, `format`, tools, or raw mode is used.

### API reproduction

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/generate -d '{
  "model": "qwen3:14b",
  "prompt": "Reply with exactly OK after thinking.",
  "think": true,
  "stream": false,
  "options": {"temperature": 0, "seed": 1, "num_predict": 2048}
}'

curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/chat -d '{
  "model": "qwen3:14b",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly OK after thinking."}],
[... log trimmed ...]
```

### Actual behavior

Observed on 2026-09-20:

```text
/api/generate
done_reason=stop
eval_count=160
response_len=752
thinking_len=0
response starts with "<think>\nOkay, the user wants me to reply..."
response contains both <think> and </think>

/api/chat
done_reason=stop
eval_count=163
[... log trimmed ...]
```

### Expected behavior

Because the request sets top-level `think: true` and the model advertises `thinking`, `/api/generate` should return the reasoning in `thinking` and the final answer in `response`, matching `/api/chat` and the documented API contract.

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### OS

Windows

### GPU

Nvidia

### CPU

Intel

### Ollama version

0.34.0

state.title: Ollama 0.12.11 Not Using GPU on RTX 5070 Ti (Blackwell/CC 12.0)
state.body:
### What is the issue?

### Description

Ollama 0.12.11 fails to detect and use the GPU for local models on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (Blackwell architecture, Compute Capability 12.0). The GPU is functional and accessible, but Ollama immediately falls back to CPU-only mode without error messages.

**Critical**: This worked before November 17, 2025, indicating a regression or compatibility issue with Blackwell architecture.

### Environment

- **OS**: Ubuntu 25.04 (GNU/Linux 6.14.0-35-generic x86_64)
- **GPU**: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (16GB VRAM)
- **GPU Compute Capability**: 12.0 (Blackwell architecture)
- **GPU Driver**: 580.95.05
- **CUDA Runtime**: 12.2.140
- **Ollama Version**: 0.12.11 (latest, clean install)
- **Installation Method**: Standalone binary via systemd service

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Ollama 0.12.11 on system with RTX 5070 Ti
2. Configure minimal systemd override:
   ```ini
   [Service]
   Environment=OLLAMA_MODELS=/mnt/shared/ollama-models/models
   Environment=CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
   ```
3. Start Ollama service: `sudo systemctl start ollama.service`
4. Load a model: `ollama run llama3.1:8b`
5. Check GPU usage: `ollama ps` or `curl http://localhost:11434/api/ps`

### Expected Behavior

- Ollama should detect GPU and initialize CUDA backend
- Models should offload layers to GPU
- `ollama ps` should show non-zero `size_vram`
- Logs should show: `ggml_cuda_init: found 1 CUDA devices` and `load_backend: loaded CUDA backend`

### Actual Behavior

- Ollama discovers GPU but immediately falls back to CPU
- All models show `size_vram: 0 MB`
- Logs show:
  ```
  msg="discovering available GPUs..."
  msg="inference compute" id=cpu library=cpu
  msg="entering low vram mode" "total vram"="0 B"
  ```
- No error messages (silent fallback)
- Models run on CPU (slow performance: ~60+ seconds for simple queries)

### Evidence It Previously Worked

**Logs from November 17, 2025** (when GPU was working):
```
ggml_cuda_init: found 1 CUDA devices
load_backend: loaded CUDA backend from /usr/local/lib/ollama/cuda_v13/libggml-cuda.so
device=GPU for model weights and KV cache
offloaded 41/41 layers to GPU
```

**After system reboot on November 18, 2025**: GPU detection stopped working.

### Troubleshooting Attempted

1. ✅ Set environment variables (`OLLAMA_NUM_GPU=1`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`)
2. ✅ Reinstalled Ollama binary (v0.12.11 from GitHub releases)
3. ✅ Manual CUDA library path configuration (`LD_LIBRARY_PATH`)
4. ✅ Created symlinks for CUDA libraries
5. ✅ **Clean install**: Complete removal of all Ollama files/configs + fresh install
6. ✅ Minimal configuration (removed all manual overrides, let Ollama auto-discover)

**Result**: All attempts show identical behavior - GPU discovery runs but immediately falls back to CPU within ~13ms.

### GPU Verification

GPU is functional and accessible:
```bash
$ nvidia-smi
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 580.95.05        [...]

state.title: Intermittent "model xxx not found" errors
state.body:
### What is the issue?

Ollama commands that reference a model (show, rm, list, etc) will occasionally fail with a "not found" error:
```console
$ ollama show laguna-s-2.1:q4_k_m
Error: model 'laguna-s-2.1:q4_k_m' not found
```
This is due to canonicalization in [`getExistingName`](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/891b0862320cf3a4d06730d03aaec10521596217/server/routes.go#L1225) using the wrong cased part when searching the existing models for a match.

Fixed in #18438.

state.title: v0.32.2 and later cause token failures when used with llama3.3:70b
state.body:
### What is the issue?

I am using Ollama and some models in tested local setup. After auto-upgrade to v0.32.2 Ollama fails to derive proper content through llama3.3:70b and generates only junk tokens (see output sample). The issue occurs in DEV and PROD, has been proven not to be caused by recent Python releases (reverted code base back several weeks for debugging the issue) and is still existent in v0.32.3 but reverting to the last good version v0.32.1 or earlier does continue to work.

All other models run well with all versions of Ollama.

Mitigation: Use v.0.32.1 or earlier and disable Ollama automatic updates.

### Relevant log output

state.title: Local /api/embed and /api/generate return "500 Internal Server Error: tokenize error: {"error":{"message":"Invalid API Key","type":"authentication_error","code":401}}
state.body:
### What is the issue?

Title: Local /api/embed and /api/generate return "tokenize error: Invalid API Key" (authentication_error, 401) with no cloud credentials configured

### Description
On a clean local setup with no Ollama Cloud sign-in, no OLLAMA_API_KEY set, and no reverse proxy in front of Ollama, both the embedding endpoint and normal chat generation fail with an authentication error that does not match llama.cpp's native error format.

### Environment
- OS: Windows 10 (19045.6466)
- Ollama: 0.32.14
- Install method: winget

### Steps to reproduce
1. `ollama pull nomic-embed-text-v2-moe` (or any embedding model)
2. `curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed -d '{"model": "nomic-embed-text-v2-moe", "input": "test"}'`
3. Observe: `{"error":"tokenize error: {\"error\":{\"message\":\"Invalid API Key\",\"type\":\"authentication_error\",\"code\":401}}"}`
4. Same result with a completely different embedding model package (toshk0/nomic-embed-text-v2-moe:Q6_K)
5. Same result with a plain chat model: `ollama run qwen3.5:0.8b` → `Error: 500 Internal Server Error: tokenize error: {"error":{"message":"Invalid API Key","type":"authentication_error","code":401}}`

### What I've ruled out
- No OLLAMA_API_KEY set (checked User and Machine env scope, cleared both)
- No Ollama Cloud credential file present (renamed/removed ~/.ollama/id_ed25519, error persists identically)
- Not model-specific (reproduces on 3 unrelated models/packages)
- Not client-specific (reproduces with raw curl, no app/client layer involved)

### Notable detail
The error body format (`"type":"authentication_error","code":401`) does not match llama-server's native plain-text `Unauthorized: Invalid API Key` output seen in other issues (e.g. #21229, #22232). This looks like a JSON error being surfaced from somewhere else in the request path, wrapped by Ollama's "tokenize error:" prefix.

state.title: Available memory calculation on AMD APU no longer takes GTT into account
state.body:
### What is the issue?

First I have to acknowledge that I understand that officially running on 780m GPU is not supported. However for some scenarios it performs better than pure CPU and in others it's perhaps more power efficient to run on the GPU.
Perhaps this could also be relevant for bigger GPUs that are supported as the patch states:
```
The solution is MI300A approach, i.e., let VRAM allocations go to GTT.
Then device and host can flexibly and effectively share memory resource.
```
However I have to admit that the last part is just my speculation.

In any case `6.10` kernel release candidates have an improved GPU memory allocation which now allows computational workloads to utilize `GTT` in addition to `VRAM` as opposed to just `VRAM` before. More details [here](https://www.phoronix.com/news/Linux-6.10-AMDKFD-Small-APUs). I believe [this](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/kernel/-/commit/89773b85599affe89dfc030aa1cb70d6ca7de4d3) to be the relevant commit.

In practice what it means is that on my laptop with 64 GB of memory I can play around with bigger models. Prior to `0.1.45` I see the following in the logs:
```
level=INFO source=types.go:71 msg="inference compute" id=0 library=rocm compute=gfx1103 driver=0.0 name=1002:15bf total="27.3 GiB" available="27.3 GiB"
```
While this is perhaps still less than what is actually available:
```
kernel: [drm] amdgpu: 8192M of VRAM memory ready
kernel: [drm] amdgpu: 27940M of GTT memory ready.
```
it still allows to work with models that are bigger than 8 GBs that still offer reasonable performance on the 780m GPU.

It would be nice to be able to continue to be able to use that extra memory in the future. Ideally being able to access `VRAM`+`GTT`, e.g. 36 GBs would be even better.

I suspect that [this commit](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/commit/b32ebb4f2990817403484d50974077a5c52a4677) introduced some changes to how available memory is calculated. Starting from `0.1.45` I see the following in the logs:
```
level=INFO source=types.go:98 msg="inference compute" id=0 library=rocm compute=gfx1103 driver=0.0 name=1002:15bf total="8.0 GiB" available="6.4 GiB"
```
The new way of calculating the available memory does a better job of determining the actual  available free memory but ideally it would be nice if would run this calculation against `VRAM`+`GTT`.

### OS

Arch (6.10.0-rc6-1-mainline) + docker container

### GPU

AMD

### CPU

AMD

### Ollama version

0.1.48-rocm

state.title: Pulling `mistral-medium-3.5` consistently fails at the SHA256 verification step.
state.body:
### What is the issue?

Pulling `mistral-medium-3.5` consistently fails at the SHA256 verification step. The blob downloads fully (80 GB) but the received digest never matches the expected one — and it changes on every attempt, suggesting the file served is corrupted or non-deterministic on the registry side.

**Steps to reproduce**

```
ollama run mistral-medium-3.5
```

**Expected behavior**

Digest verification passes and the model runs.

**Actual behavior**

### Relevant log output

```shell
Error: digest mismatch, file must be downloaded again:
  want sha256:a46088eccd0d171cc2694f315f2921bd0fda0ae3577099c4864cbe98f190807e
  got  sha256:579e02e55f9a5aa5d58555dfdca243a6e5b340b24952084a0033edb477c4cf5a  (attempt 1)
  got  sha256:6392b4583c9fbb874a811066019b53e58287825f9f71b367d1c2404441bdb11e  (attempt 2)
  got  sha256:979a51453133ccca9f4bb67034b35b579925a89920df3a90f2fcfc6bee4ef5e8  (attempt 3)

The received digest is **different on every attempt**, which rules out a local corruption issue. The problem appears to be on the registry side.

**Environment**
- OS: Windows 11
[... log trimmed ...]
```

Windows

Nvidia

state.title: Feature Request: Include usage metrics in streaming chat responses
state.body:
## Problem Description

Currently, the OpenAPI spec defines `ChatStreamEvent` without the usage/metrics fields that are available in the non-streaming `ChatResponse`. This creates an inconsistency where developers cannot access important performance metrics (token counts, timing information) during streaming responses.

## Proposed Solution

Add the following fields to `ChatStreamEvent` in the OpenAPI spec to match `ChatResponse`:

- `total_duration` - Total request duration in nanoseconds
- `load_duration` - Model loading duration in nanoseconds  
- `prompt_eval_count` - Number of tokens in the prompt
- `prompt_eval_duration` - Time spent evaluating the prompt in nanoseconds
- `eval_count` - Number of tokens in the response
- `eval_duration` - Time spent generating response in nanoseconds

Additionally, add `logprobs` to `ChatStreamEvent` since it's present in `GenerateStreamEvent` but missing from the chat streaming spec.

## Use Case

Developers need real-time token usage and timing data during streaming to:
- Display token counts to users in real-time
- Monitor model performance and latency
- Implement rate limiting based on actual usage
- Debug performance issues

## Implementation Suggestion

The Go implementation already uses a single `ChatResponse` struct for both streaming and non-streaming responses (see `api/types.go`). The fix primarily requires updating the OpenAPI spec in `docs/api.md` to include the metrics fields in `ChatStreamEvent`.

Reference: A similar pattern is already implemented for `GenerateStreamEvent` which correctly includes these metrics.

## Additional Context

This would also resolve the inconsistency noted in issue #14680 regarding the mismatch between streaming and non-streaming response schemas.

state.title: Linux tips-  sharing models directory with Msty
state.body:
I had a lot of head scratching getting Msty to share the Ollama models directory and retain normal Ollama functions. 

Posting my process here in the hopes of helping others get the job done.

First you're going to need to create a folder for the models in your systems /home folder but **not in your users home folder** go up a level.

`sudo mkdir /home/.ollama_models` 

give the directory to ollama user and group

`sudo chown ollama:ollama /home/.ollama_models`

and modify it's permissions to be readable by all users

`sudo chmod -R a+r /home/.ollama_models`

next modify the ollama.service environment variables with 

`sudo systemctl edit ollama.service`

This will open a temporary overrides file for the ollama.service. Read what it says and enter in the top section.

`[Service]`
`Environment="OLLAMA_MODELS=/home/.ollama_models"`

write out, confirm and quit the editor then

`sudo systemctl daemon-reload`
`sudo systemctl restart ollama`

confirm your override is being applied and the service is running with `sudo systemctl status ollama.service`

Now you can point Msty to the models folder and it should restart the Local AI service.

At this point I had to close Msty and reopen it and it was ready to go and detected the model I had pulled with Ollama.

1. `if` statement without an condition: You have an `if` statement without any condition. An `if` statement should always have a condition to check whether the statement inside the `if` block should be executed or not. For example, you could replace the `if` statement with `if (x > 0)` to make^C

state.title: Documentation best practice for Modelfile system prompts — HADS standard
state.body:
Wanted to flag an open standard that could help Ollama users write better system prompts and documentation: **HADS** — Human-AI Document Standard.

https://github.com/catcam/hads

**The idea:** Tag sections of your docs so the model knows what to read and skip:
- `**[SPEC]**` — facts to extract (terse, bullet lists)
- `**[NOTE]**` — human context (model can skip)
- `**[BUG]**` — known failures + fixes (always read)

An AI manifest at the top makes it explicit. Works in Modelfile `SYSTEM` blocks, knowledge docs, any Markdown.

**Especially useful for smaller models** (7B-13B) — they don't have to reason about document structure, the manifest tells them exactly what matters.

Worth a mention in Ollama docs or community resources?

state.title: [Docs/Code] Clarify supported architectures for Flash Attention and KV Cache Quantization
state.body:
Hi Team,

I have been analyzing the source code to optimize memory usage for deployments on constrained GPUs (e.g., Nvidia L4), specifically looking into `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION` and `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE`.

I noticed that while the [FAQ](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/faq.md) mentions how to enable these features via environment variables, it does not explicitly list which model architectures are actually supported.

Upon reviewing `fs/ggml/ggml.go`, I found that `FlashAttention()` relies on a specific allowlist:

```go
// fs/ggml/ggml.go
func (f GGML) FlashAttention() bool {
    return slices.Contains([]string{
        "gemma3",
        "gptoss", "gpt-oss",
        "mistral3",
        "qwen3", "qwen3moe",
        "qwen3vl", "qwen3vlmoe",
    }, f.KV().String("general.architecture"))
}
```

**The Issue:**
Developers might attempt to force `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0` on architectures like `command-r` or `llama3` (standard), expecting memory savings. However, because these architectures are not in the allowlist (or `SupportsFlashAttention` returns false), the server silently falls back to `f16`, leading to unexpected OOMs or higher VRAM usage than calculated.

It would be very helpful to add a small table or note in `docs/faq.md` or `docs/gpu.md` listing the architectures that currently support Flash Attention (and thus KV Quantization).

This would save developers significant time when debugging memory usage and planning capacity for specific models.

I hope its get understood. By the way , im interested to add or mainatin that table in `docs/faq.mdx` file whenever a new model gets added in `FalshAttention` function of `fs/ggml/ggml.go` file.

Is there a clear distinctions as what options should be used by either the chat or the embedding endpoint? And conversely what are not?

state.title: Fix: bind: address already in use + 403 from Chrome Extension (macOS)
state.body:
If you run:

```bash
OLLAMA_ORIGINS="<your_url>" ollama serve
```
and get:

```bash
Error: listen tcp 127.0.0.1:11434: bind: address already in use
```

It means the Ollama LaunchAgent is already running and auto-respawning the daemon.

1. Check if Ollama LaunchAgent is active

```bash
launchctl list | grep -i ollama
```

You’ll likely see:

```bash
com.ollama.ollama
```

2. Remove the LaunchAgent

```bash
launchctl remove com.ollama.ollama
```

3. Verify port 11434 is free

```bash
lsof -i :11434
```

If nothing prints, the port is free.

4. Start Ollama manually with CORS enabled
```bash
OLLAMA_ORIGINS="<your_url>*,http://localhost:*" ollama serve
```

Leave this terminal running.

5. Verify CORS works

In another terminal:
```bash

curl -i http://localhost:11434/api/tags \
  -H "Origin: <your_url>"

```
You should see:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <your_url>
```

state.title: [Docs] Incorrect default value for num_predict?
state.body:
The API documentation (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api.md#generate-a-chat-completion) refers to https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/modelfile.md#valid-parameters-and-values for more information about the parameters that can be specified in the `options` field of a chat completion request.

However, the default value for the `num_predict` parameter described there either doesn't apply to calls made via the python library (in which case the docs should emphasise this) or is incorrect.

For `num_predict`, the docs say:

> Maximum number of tokens to predict when generating text. (Default: 128, -1 = infinite generation, -2 = fill context)

I initially wondered how Ollama could generate responses much longer than 128 tokens (without me specifying a value for the parameter). After adding a debug statement in `router.go`, I noticed that the server received a value of -1 for `num_predict`, which matches my previous observations.

As a consequence, the documentation is either misleading or gives an incorrect default value.

state.title: EU AI Act Compliance: Documentation for Risk-Sensitive Deployments
state.body:
## Context

Ollama enables running LLMs locally, which is excellent for data privacy. However, when deploying Ollama in production for sensitive use cases (content filtering, automated decision-making), EU AI Act compliance becomes relevant.

## Proposed Addition

1. **Deployment Risk Assessment**: Guide to determine if your use case requires compliance checks
   - Interactive decision tree: Is this high-risk? (recruitment, law enforcement, etc.)
   - Links to EU AI Act definitions

2. **Audit & Monitoring**: Best practices for deployments requiring compliance
   - Input/output logging recommendations
   - Model version tracking
   - Performance monitoring across demographics

## Example Use Case

A small company deploying Ollama for customer support should understand:
- When to use it safely
- When compliance checks are needed

## Reference

Free scanning tool available at https://arkforge.fr/mcp for developers checking compliance requirements.

state.title: Improve error reporting with old or missing AMD driver on windows (unable to load amdhip64_6.dll)
state.body:
I was trying to solve this issue that prevented me from using AMD GPU

```
time=2024-08-30T09:43:00.852-05:00 level=DEBUG source=amd_windows.go:33 msg="unable to load amdhip64_6.dll, 
please make sure to upgrade to the latest amd driver: The specified module could not be found."
```

Compared with the message for searching Nvidia, the AMD message is really minimal, here is the Nvidia output

```
time=2024-08-30T09:43:00.768-05:00 level=DEBUG source=gpu.go:469 msg="Searching for GPU library" name=cudart64_*.dll
time=2024-08-30T09:43:00.768-05:00 level=DEBUG source=gpu.go:488 msg="gpu library search" globs="[C:\\Program Files\\NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit\\CUDA\\v12.2\\bin\\cudart64_*.dll* ..........]"
```

As you can see, ollama does not tell where it tries to find `amdhip64_6`.  https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/3418#issuecomment-2253379050 said the DLL should be in ` C:\Windows\system32\amdhip64_6.dll`, which is not the case as my dll is in `C:\Program Files\AMD\ROCm\6.1\bin`. It turns out that ollama uses the environment variable `PATH` to search for the DLL, which is not very clear just by reading the console debug output. To help future users, I'd like to suggest the following improvements:

1. Print out the search path when searching for AMD GPU (like the Nvidia log above)
2. Suppress Nvidia message when `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1` and AMD message when  `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1` to simplify the log (there is no need to print out the search path if one does not need Nvidia or AMD driver)

state.title: [Feature Request] Add OpenCL and OpenBLAS support for broader hardware compatibility
state.body:
Description:
I am a user with older/limited hardware ([GT 710M 1GB, Intel HD 4000]) and would like to run local LLMs efficiently. Currently, Ollama/GPT4All primarily supports acceleration via CUDA (NVIDIA), ROCm (AMD), and Metal (Apple), which excludes many integrated and older discrete GPUs that only have OpenCL drivers.

Proposed Solution:
Integrate the OpenCL and OpenBLAS backends from the upstream llama.cpp project. The OpenCL backend in llama.cpp (-DGGML_OPENCL=ON) already provides good cross-platform support for Adreno, older Intel HD Graphics, and many other GPUs. OpenBLAS (-DLLAMA_BLAS=ON -DLLAMA_BLAS_VENDOR=OpenBLAS) can significantly accelerate CPU inference, which is crucial when GPU memory is insufficient.

This would make the project accessible to a much wider range of users with non-mainstream or legacy hardware.

My Use Case:
- Hardware: Hybrid graphics, NVIDIA GT 710M 1GB + Intel HD 4000).
- Driver/OS: NVIDIA driver 388.xx on Windows 10 and 390xx Linux.
- Current Limitation: Vulkan support is unstable, CUDA is not optimal for this old GPU. OpenCL is the only viable cross-platform compute API that works.
- Trying to use Functiongemma 270m

Additional context:
- The llama.cpp project, which underpins these tools, already has stable OpenCL and BLAS backends.
- An issue requesting OpenCL support for Ollama already exists (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/7536), indicating community interest.
- For users with weak or no dedicated GPU, CPU acceleration via BLAS libraries is often the only performant option.

state.title: Proposal: add Intel oneAPI (SYCL) backend for Intel GPUs
state.body:
### Proposal: add an Intel oneAPI (SYCL) backend for Intel GPUs

  Problem
Ollama currently accelerates Intel Arc / Iris Xe GPUs through the Vulkan
backend. On Intel GPUs, SYCL (via Level Zero and oneDNN) is the native,
fully-featured compute stack: it supports XMX matrix units, fp16 matmul,
and 33/33-layer offload on Arc (measured ~150 tok/s on Arc B580 with a
1.8B Q4_K_M model). Vulkan does not expose these paths as completely.

  Proposed change
Add `sycl` to `OLLAMA_LLAMA_BACKENDS` so the Windows build can link the
SYCL llama.cpp backend (`ggml-sycl.dll`) and bundle the oneAPI runtime
(oneDNN / oneMKL / Level Zero adapters) into the installed payload, the
same way CUDA/ROCm/Vulkan backends are handled today.

  Scope (4 commits, ~156 lines, 6 files):
- `cmake/` + `llama/server`: enable the SYCL llama.cpp backend via Ninja,
  using MSVC `cl` for C and Intel DPC++ `icx` for C++
- `discover/` + `ml/` + `envconfig/`: detect SYCL devices from llama-server
  output and allow `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR` for multi-GPU selection

How it will be used
Users build with `-DOLLAMA_LLAMA_BACKENDS=sycl` on Windows and run Ollama
normally; the model is offloaded to the Intel GPU through Level Zero.

How it will be tested
Built and verified on Windows 11 with Arc B580: device auto-detection,
`ollama run` with full GPU offload, and runtime bundle (no oneAPI needed on
the target machine). GitHub Actions workflow builds the Windows SYCL package
and runs it in CI.

Note on new dependencies
No new external dependency for Ollama itself: the SYCL backend already
exists in the pinned llama.cpp; this change only plumbs it through the
superbuild and device discovery.

state.title: Allow Control List for AI Models Downloaded
state.body:
I work as a sys-admin at a University and there is a growing demand for using Ollama in computer labs for teaching. There are a few considerations we have for faciliating AI models in Labs.
- Due to data governance policies, we have to consider what Student data is uploaded to cloud services. This limits the kind of models we use on local machines.
- We need to ensure we are working inline with the licence terms of a given AI model, the licences seem to vary between models and we don't have the ability to control what model is downloaded.
- To optimise performance, we would likely want to have the models installed locally on the machine rather than in user profiles.

This feels like a big ask and is more than one feature, but I was keen to better understand whether the following was a consideration for development:

- Models stored on local disks rather than user profile (located on network shares). This would optimise read/write locally but also mean models aren't being downloaded from servers by individual users, reducing duplicating data and saving bandwidth.
- ACL type feature to limit which models are downloaded and limit to approved models.

Thanks in advance

state.title: Expose `max_soft_tokens` (image token budget) as a runtime parameter for Gemma 4 models
state.body:
Gemma 4's vision encoder supports a variable-resolution token budget via `max_soft_tokens`, but this value is currently hardcoded to `280` in `model/models/gemma4/process_image.go` ([see L25–31](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/7d271e6dc9fb114d48b91a1ed2ed3d414178a883/model/models/gemma4/process_image.go#L25-L31)). There is no way to override it at runtime through the API or via ollama-python library.

Google's own documentation for Gemma 4 explicitly recommends tuning this budget for OCR tasks that require higher image resolution:
https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/capabilities/vision/image#variable_resolution_token_budget

The default budget of 280 tokens is insufficient for fine-grained visual tasks. In practice, this causes measurable accuracy regressions. A concrete example using license plate recognition with `gemma4-e4b`:

| Configuration | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Ollama default (280 token budget) | `YRSGNB` | `YRSGNBY` |
| HuggingFace Transformers with `max_soft_tokens=560` | `YRSGNBY` ✓ | `YRSGNBY` |

The same degradation is reproducible with the unquantized model when the budget is left at the default, even affecting higher parameter model variants such as 27B. Please refer to this discussion  https://github.com/ollama/ollama-python/issues/651.

state.title: Feature Request: Include Model Context Length in /v1/models Response
state.body:
## Problem Statement

Currently, querying the OpenAI-compatible endpoint via GET /v1/models returns a basic list of model IDs and creation timestamps, but omits important metadata like the maximum context length:
```Bash
curl https://ollama.com/v1/models
```
```JSON
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "gemma4:31b",
      "object": "model",
      "created": 1775149200,
      "owned_by": "ollama"
    }
  ]
}
```
To find the context length or architecture specs, users are forced to make a separate native API call (POST /api/show) for every individual model. This creates unnecessary friction for client applications and developers trying to dynamically configure token limits.

## Proposed Solution

Enhance the OpenAI-compatible /v1/models (and optionally /v1/models/{model}) endpoint to include context window metadata (such as context_length or OpenAI-style extensions like max_model_len) directly within the model object payload.

For example:
```JSON
{
  "id": "gemma4:31b",
  "object": "model",
  "created": 1775149200,
  "owned_by": "ollama",
  "context_length": 262144
}
```

state.title: 【Feature Request】Windows版本增加对AMD R9显卡（gfx1201）的支持
state.body:
## 功能描述（Feature Description）
建议Windows 11版本尽快增加对AMD R9系列显卡的官方支持，重点实现对gfx1201架构显卡的兼容适配，确保该架构显卡能正常识别、稳定运行，并充分发挥硬件性能，解决目前该系列显卡无法被识别、运行异常或性能无法释放的问题。

其中，gfx1201架构对应AMD RDNA 4核心，涵盖Radeon R9系列相关型号（如Radeon AI Pro R9700）及同架构衍生显卡，该架构显卡具备较强的图形处理和计算能力，当前Windows版本暂未实现对其的有效支持，影响相关用户的正常使用体验。

## 需求背景与使用场景（Background & Use Cases）

随着AMD R9系列gfx1201架构显卡的普及（如Radeon AI Pro R9700等型号），越来越多Windows用户开始使用该类显卡进行AI部署场景。但目前Windows版本的软件/系统组件暂未适配该架构显卡，导致出现以下问题：

- AI 模型推理时，显卡无法被正常识别加载；

- 即使手动改成Vulkan方案，AI推理计算及其不稳定，出现启动失败、闪退或功能灰色不可用的情况；

- 部分场景下AI计算，即使勉强运行，也会出现性能严重损耗问题，无法发挥gfx1201架构的硬件优势。

典型使用场景包括：

1. 专业用户使用Radeon AI Pro R9700等gfx1201架构显卡进行本地AI模型部署，需要软件充分调用显卡计算资源；

2. 工作站用户采用多卡（如2张Radeon AI Pro R9700）配置，用于高性能计算场景，需系统/软件对该架构显卡提供完善的多卡支持。

## 预期效果（Expected Behavior）

1. Ollama Windows版本软件/系统能正确识别AMD R9系列gfx1201架构显卡， 正确加载模型到GPU进行计算；

2. 显卡驱动能正常加载，软件可稳定调用显卡资源，无启动失败、闪退、卡顿等异常情况；

3. 充分适配gfx1201架构特性，确保显卡性能正常释放，AI计算场景下的性能表现与硬件规格匹配；

4. 支持多卡配置（如Radeon AI Pro R9700多卡堆叠）的正常识别与协同工作，满足工作站高性能计算需求；

5. 适配AMD官方最新驱动，确保后续驱动更新后仍能保持良好的兼容性。

希望开发团队能重视该需求，尽快推进AMD R9系列gfx1201显卡的适配工作，提升Windows版本的兼容性和用户体验，感谢！

Labels: enhancement, windows, gpu-support, amd-r9

state.title: Support `--resume` and `--continue` flag for resuming Claude Code sessions launched via `ollama launch claude`
state.body:
### Problem
- When launching Claude Code with `ollama launch` and then exiting, attempting to resume the session with a `--resume` flag fails:
  - Error observed: `Error: unknown flag: --resume`
- This prevents reattaching to interactive code sessions, breaking workflows that expect long-lived, resumable development sessions.

### Why this change matters
- Resumable sessions are essential for developer productivity....users often start a session, do work, exit the client, and later want to reattach to the same context without losing state.
- Without a resume mechanism, users would have to recreate session/conversation (files, context, conversation history), which leads to context flow break and reduces adoption of the interactive Claude Code experience in Ollama.

### How the change will be used
- CLI usage example:
    - `ollama launch claude --resume <session_id> or ollama launch claude --continue`
  - Expected behavior:
    - The CLI recognizes the `--resume` flag or `resume` subcommand.
    - It locates the session, re-establishes the program state, and restores the interactive context (conversation history, open files, relevant model state).
    - If the session cannot be resumed (expired, missing, incompatible), a clear error message is returned with guidance.

state.title: Promote ollama parallel capacity
state.body: I know ollama use only one whole GPU to calculate, other GPU only contribute VRAM for storage, but not work. If I set 2 parallel tasks, that means all 2 tasks both run on GPU1, while GPU2 is free. I suggest to allocate whole kv-cache in single GPU and deliver different percent of ANN network in all GPU, eg: 128k ctx (100%kv-cache) and 40% ANN are allocated in GPU1, 128k ctx (100%kv-cache) 60% ANN are allocated in GPU2 (different GPU style). When session1 come, the task can be set to ollama process on GPU1 with whole 128k ctx, then session2 can be set to GPU2 with the same settings. Now the two GPUs can all be used.

state.title: Ollama Cloud - Add context limit information to the /api/tags response
state.body:
Right now, [the /api/tags endpoint on Ollama Cloud](https://ollama.com/api/tags) returns model metadata but it does not include context limits. Tools like Goose have to maintain their own mappings within their code since it's not currently available on the API response.

If the API could return those limits along with the models, it would be a big win for using new models. New model discovery is currently easy, so if context limits for the models were as well then downstream agents could make use of them much more seamlessly.

state.title: ROCm backend fails to initialize on AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (RDNA4, gfx1201) in Windows 11
state.body:
**Description**

I am using Ollama v0.17.7 on Windows 11 with an **AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700** (RDNA4 architecture, gfx1201). The ROCm backend fails to initialize, falling back to CPU, even though the HIP SDK 7.1 is installed and the Vulkan backend works perfectly.

**Environment**

* OS: Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)
* Ollama version: 0.17.7 (installed in `C:\Ollama`)
* GPU: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (2x, 32GB GDDR6 each) – RDNA4, gfx1201
* Driver: AMD Software Pro Edition 26.2.2 (driver date 2026/2/17)
* HIP SDK: 7.1.0 installed (AMD HIP SDK components)
* ROCm files used: `ollama-windows-amd64-rocm.zip` (extracted to `C:\Ollama\lib\ollama\`)

**Expected Behavior**Ollama should initialize the ROCm backend and utilize the GPU(s) for inference.

**Actual Behavior**Ollama detects the GPU (`description="AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700" compute=gfx1201`) but then logs `filtering device which didn't fully initialize` and falls back to CPU. The inference compute log shows only CPU.

**Steps Already Taken**

1. Installed latest AMD driver and HIP SDK 7.1.
2. Set `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1` and `OLLAMA_DEBUG=1`.
3. Replaced `ollama.exe` with the one from `ollama-windows-amd64.zip` and copied ROCm libraries from `ollama-windows-amd64-rocm.zip` to `C:\Ollama\lib\ollama\`.
4. Tried `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=12.0.1`, `12.0.0`, `11.0.0` – all result in the same filtering.
5. Vulkan backend (`OLLAMA_VULKAN=1`) works fine, utilizing both GPUs (see logs below).

**Relevant Logs** (from `ollama serve` with `OLLAMA_DEBUG=1`)

    time=2026-03-07T09:49:00.849+08:00 level=DEBUG source=runner.go:153 msg="filtering device which didn't fully initialize" id=0 libdir=C:\Ollama\lib\ollama\rocm pci_id=0000:07:00.0 library=ROCm
    time=2026-03-07T09:49:00.850+08:00 level=INFO source=types.go:60 msg="inference compute" id=cpu library=cpu ...

The Vulkan backend successfully enumerates both GPUs:

    ggml_vulkan: Found 3 Vulkan devices:
    ggml_vulkan: 0 = AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (AMD proprietary driver) | uma: 0 | fp16: 1 | bf16: 1 | warp size: 64 | shared memory: 32768 | int dot: 1 | matrix cores: KHR_coopmat
    ...

**Analysis**The ROCm libraries bundled with Ollama (version 6.x, as indicated by `amdhip64_6.dll`) do not include precompiled kernels for `gfx1201` (RDNA4). The `TensileLibrary_*` files from the ROCm 6.2 build path (as seen in the user's attached file list) contain kernels only up to `gfx1151`. Thus, even with `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION`, the HIP runtime cannot find suitable kernels for this architecture, leading to initialization failure.

**Request**Please update the Windows ROCm support in Ollama to include `gfx1201` (RDNA4). This could be achieved by:

* Bundling a newer version of ROCm (e.g., 7.x) that adds support for RDNA4.
* Adding the necessary kernel builds for `gfx1201` to the existing ROCm 6.x package.

Thank you for your work on Ollama! I'm happy to provide any additional information or testing if needed.

---

state.title: Feature Request: Stream tool call arguments in anthropic/anthropic.go:Process() to avoid triggering a Claude Code timeout
state.body:
# Environment
* Ollama 0.17.7 + a patch for https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/14816
* Claude Code 2.1.70
* OS/hardware: Ubuntu 24.04, AMD Ryzen 5, GeForce RTX 3060

If it matters, I'm running everything locally, ethernet cable unplugged.

```
$ ollama ps
NAME                    ID              SIZE     PROCESSOR          CONTEXT    UNTIL               
glm-4.7-flash:latest    d1a8a26252f1    21 GB    46%/54% CPU/GPU    65536      59 minutes from now
```

# Reproduction
## Disclaimer
I don't have a good, simple repro case - I'm not great at getting LLMs to do exactly what I want, so provoking the problematic behavior is hit or miss. What I'm trying to do is to get Claude to write out a long-ish file (specifically, something that takes more than ~255 seconds to generate the tool call for). Claude sometimes tries to do other things (e.g. search the web, or summarize the story) before writing out the file; I'm not sure how those interact but was trying to avoid them to keep things simple. Reproducing this might require some retries or prompt fiddling, but **any way of generating a lot of text as a tool call argument should work**, I'm just not sure how to capture that concisely.

## Steps
1. Run a local Ollama build: `<various Ollama env vars> go run . serve`
2. Run Claude Code `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="" claude --model glm-4.7-flash`
3. At the prompt, enter something like `Write the public domain short story "Luck" by Mark Twain to luck.txt.`

While this is sufficient to reproduce the behavior on my system, the underlying issue is a timeout; a more powerful computer might be able to successfully complete the task quickly enough. Setting `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""` to force CPU inference or specifying a longer text should make the issue more obvious.

## Expected behavior
luck.txt should be created and contain text.

## Observed behavior
When the request finishes, `grep ERROR ~/.claude/debug/latest` shows `[ERROR] Error streaming, falling back to non-streaming mode: The operation timed out.`. No file is created.

# Observations
https://ollama.com/blog/streaming-tool initially made me think this was expected to work, but reading it more closely I see that it only talks about streaming tool *responses*, not composing the *arguments*, so I'm filing this as a feature request instead of as a bug.

## Packet trace behavior
When I've been able to get this to reproduce (which is not 100%), inspecting a packet trace suggests that Claude's streaming timeout seems to be about 255 seconds since the last content block was received. Looking at port 11434 (i.e. Claude accessing Ollama), the thinking block is streamed as expected, but then the stream pauses when it reaches the tool call - there are still keep-alive packets being exchanged, but no content block deltas. Looking at the other interesting TCP stream (which I believe is Ollama internally talking to the LLM), I see that it's in the middle  [...]
